notes:
POC focus: Dedicated capacity performance benchmarking and sizing for highly regulated clinical chat + retrieval.

Summary / ask:
- Veridian needs throughput guarantees and latency SLOs for patient-facing conversational triage (low-latency for short-turn responses, longer tails OK for long summaries).
- Primary decision hinge: Can Redwood Dedicated deliver predictable p95/p99 at scale and provide committed GPU reservations with SLA credits?

Key requirements (from CTO / Head of ML infra):
- Workloads: clinical-chat (short form Q->A), embeddings for patient record search, post-visit summarization (longer outputs).
- Latency targets: median < 180ms for <128-token chat responses; p95 < 350ms, p99 < 900ms at 80% steady-state load.
- Throughput: sustained platform-level throughput target ~45k tokens/sec (aggregate across 24h), spikes to 120k tokens/sec for surge events.
- Error budget: <0.5% 5xx errors, <1% timeouts.
- Residency/compliance: data residency in us-east; HIPAA controls, KMS-integration required, full audit logging.

POC plan (technical):
- Fixtures: representative prompt set provided by Veridian (clinic dialogues, 3k anonymized notes for embedding tests, 120 long documents for summarization).
- Models: redwood-4x-32k (primary), compact variant for fallback. Quantization experiments to int8/4-bit for cost tradeoffs.
- Hardware candidates: baseline: 4xH100-80GB; target sizing: 8xH100 or 12xA100-80GB depending on batch behavior.
- Load tests: step-ramp to target RPS using Locust/k6; ramp schedule: 0->50% (30m), 50->80% (30m), step to 100% (1h), sustain 80% for 72h soak. Short spike tests to 200% for 15m to validate burst policies.
- Metrics to capture: p50/p95/p99 latency, tail latency distribution per seq-length bucket, tokens/sec, GPU utilization, GPU memory fragmentation / OOMs, KV cache hit rate, batching efficiency, concurrency, error rates, autoscale latency (time to add nodes), failover to fallback model latency/behavior.
- Acceptance criteria: pass 72h soak with p95/p99 within targets, <0.5% 5xx, no OOMs, cache hit >= 60% on retrieval workload, autoscale reflex <120s to double capacity, documented fallback behavior.

Representative prompts (anonymized examples):
- "Patient: I've had chest tightness for 2 hours and shortness of breath. What should I do?" -> chat response target ~40-100 tokens.
- "Summarize today's consult note and list recommended follow-ups." -> summarization target 300-800 tokens.
- Embedding query: free-text search against 3M sentence vectors, top-k latency goal < 75ms for embeddings-based rerank.

Preliminary bench notes (from Redwood lab):
- 4xH100 baseline (lab config): chat workload (<=128 tokens): p95=210ms, p99=680ms at 2k RPS equivalent (server-side batching enabled).
- Embeddings throughput: 18k vectors/sec per H100 with optimized kernel; retrieval latencies dominated by kNN infra, not model.
- Observed batching improvement: continuous batching improved tokens/sec by ~30% for median batched request patterns.

Negotiation items flagged by Veridian procurement/security:
- SLA: request 99.95% uptime for dedicated cluster + specific latency SLOs with financial credits.
- Reserved capacity contract length options: 12 vs 24 months; want burst credits and defined scale-up windows.
- Support: premium on-call SE during the 72h soak and first 30 days post-commit.

Quotes / call snippets:
- CTO: "We can tolerate occasional long tails, but median must feel instant for patients — anything above 200ms median will degrade UX."
- Head of Infra: "If you can't guarantee no OOMs during our worst-case weekend run, we can't sign."

Risks / unknowns:
- Network egress policy for on-prem connector needs legal review.
- Final hardware SKU (H100 vs A100) dependent on lab soak outcomes and costs.

Next steps (short):
- Redwood to run 72h soak on dedicated trial cluster (start 2026-03-15).
- Veridian to provide full anonymized sample set and kNN index snapshot by 2026-03-12.
- SE (Rita) to join soak monitoring + weekly sync.
- Procurement to review draft SLA and propose redlines by 2026-03-22.
